import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Department': [
        'Family Practice', 'Family Practice', 'Family Practice', 'Radiology', 'Radiology', 'Radiology',
        'Various', 'Various', 'Internal Medicine', 'Internal Medicine', 'Internal Medicine', 'Internal Medicine',
        'Surgery', 'Surgery', 'ICU', 'ICU', 'ICU', 'Post-Op Unit', 'Post-Op Unit', 'Rehabilitation',
        'Rehabilitation', 'Rehabilitation', 'Rehabilitation', 'Social Work', 'Home Health', 'Primary Care',
        'Primary Care', 'Primary Care', 'Primary Care'
    ],
    'Stage': [
        'Initial Consultation', 'Initial Consultation', 'Initial Consultation',
        'Diagnostic Testing', 'Diagnostic Testing', 'Diagnostic Testing',
        'Referral Processing', 'Referral Processing',
        'Inpatient Admission', 'Inpatient Admission', 'Inpatient Admission', 'Pre-Surgical Prep',
        'Surgery/Procedure', 'Surgery/Procedure',
        'ICU Monitoring', 'ICU Monitoring', 'ICU Monitoring',
        'Post-Op Recovery', 'Post-Op Recovery',
        'Rehabilitation Start', 'Rehabilitation Progress', 'Rehabilitation Progress', 'Rehabilitation Progress',
        'Discharge Planning',
        'Home Transition',
        'Full Recovery', 'Follow-Up Visit', 'Final Check-Up', 'Final Check-Up'
    ],
    'Cost': [
        250, 260, 240, 2000, 2200, 2150, 2800, 3200, 4500, 4800, 5000, 7500,
        20000, 22000, 48000, 50000, 52000, 64000, 66000, 80000, 95000, 97000, 98000,
        105000, 120000, 130000, 140000, 145000, 150000
    ],
    'Duration': [
        7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7,
        14, 14, 14, 14, 14, 7, 30, 7, 7, 7
    ],
    'PatientVolume': [
        1000, 980, 990, 900, 880, 910, 850, 870, 800, 790, 770, 720,
        650, 660, 580, 560, 590, 520, 500, 450, 400, 395, 385,
        350, 320, 300, 280, 260, 250
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="pastel")

boxplot = sns.boxplot(
    x='Department',
    y='Cost',
    hue='Duration',
    data=df[df['Department'] != 'Rehabilitation'],
    dodge=True,
    width=0.6,
    fliersize=5,
    linewidth=2
)

plt.title('Distribution of Patient Volume by Department and Treatment Stage', fontsize=14, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Medical Department', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Cost per Patient ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.legend(title='Duration (Days)', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')
===  summary.txt
This chart is a box plot that illustrates the distribution of patient costs across various medical departments, segmented by treatment duration. The title of the chart, "Distribution of Patient Costs by Department and Treatment Duration," is prominently displayed at the top. The x-axis represents the different medical departments, including Family Practice, Radiology, Various, Internal Medicine, Surgery, ICU, Post-Op Unit, Rehabilitation, Social Work, Home Health, and Primary Care. The y-axis shows the cost per patient in dollars, ranging from 0 to 150,000.

The chart uses three distinct shades of grey to differentiate between treatment durations of 7 days, 14 days, and 30 days, as indicated by the legend on the right side. Each box plot within the departments displays the median, quartiles, and potential outliers of patient costs. For example, in the Family Practice department, costs for a 7-day duration are minimal, clustering around $250 with little variation. Radiology and Various departments also show low costs for 7-day treatments, with values around $2,000 to $3,000.

Internal Medicine exhibits slightly higher costs, with a noticeable spread around $4,500 to $7,500 for 7-day treatments. Surgery costs for the same duration range approximately from $20,000 to $22,000. The ICU department shows a much higher cost distribution, with values around $48,000 to $52,000 for 7-day treatments. Post-Op Unit costs for 7 days are around $64,000 to $66,000.

Rehabilitation displays costs for both 14-day and 7-day durations, with 14-day treatments clustering around $80,000 to $98,000 and 7-day treatments showing a single data point around $105,000. The Home Health department has one significant outlier at $120,000 for a 30-day treatment. Lastly, the Primary Care department shows a range of costs for 7-day treatments, from around $130,000 to $150,000, with some variability and potential outliers. The overall visualization effectively highlights the variance in patient costs across departments and treatment durations.
